text:
Ammonia, hypoxanthine, and uric acid are the ADP-degradation products that rise in the blood during multiple-sprint exercise. Repeated sprints drive adenylate kinase and AMP deaminase, releasing ammonia, while hypoxanthine leaves muscle and is oxidized to uric acid, so both accumulate in plasma. Urea is only a later hepatic product of that ammonia, and creatine and creatinine come from the phosphocreatine pool.
CONFIDENCE: 86
